question: Is there a deadlock in this resource-allocation graph? R3 has two instances, so does the cycle really mean deadlock?
reference_answer: Edges: P1 -> R1 (request), R1 -> P2 (assigned), P2 -> R2 (request), R2 -> P3 (assigned), P3 -> R3 (request), R3 -> P1 and R3 -> P2 (one instance each). So P1 holds an R3 instance and waits for R1; P2 holds R1 and an R3 instance and waits for R2; P3 holds R2 and waits for R3. Cycles: P1 -> R1 -> P2 -> R2 -> P3 -> R3 -> P1 and P2 -> R2 -> P3 -> R3 -> P2. With several instances a cycle alone is not enough, but here both R3 instances are held by P1 and P2, which are themselves blocked, and nothing is free (available = 0, 0, 0): no process can finish and release anything, so P1, P2 and P3 are deadlocked.
